memory_update.text: RHI Magnesita via U.S. OTC ticker RHHMY is the most direct U.S.-accessible public proxy for Indian refractory consolidation, but the cleanest operating data likely sits at RHI Magnesita India, listed locally in India.
Vesuvius via U.S. OTC ticker CKSNF is a second direct refractory/flow-control supplier to track, especially for steel flow-control and service-led switching-cost evidence in India.
MTX is the cleanest U.S.-exchange underfollowed mid-cap with refractory systems exposure, but India-specific exposure remains a verification gap.
ArcelorMittal should be treated as a customer/demand anchor through AM/NS India expansion, not as a supplier-side beneficiary of refractory consolidation.
The node has limited pure-play U.S.-listed coverage; later layers should decide whether OTC names and local Indian listings are allowed or whether the investable U.S. universe is too indirect.

RHHMY is the cleanest US-accessible candidate for the Indian refractory consolidation node because it maps directly to RHI Magnesita's refractory products, steel/cement end markets, India exposure and listed Indian subsidiary.
CKSNY should remain in the underfollowed lane as a US OTC ADR for Vesuvius, with direct relevance to steel flow-control consumables, advanced refractories and an Indian listed subsidiary.

CODYY is a reference anchor, not a pure underfollowed name, because Saint-Gobain's India refractory opportunity is buried inside a large diversified group but supported by a specific Shinagawa-Grindwell Norton blast-furnace partnership.

Several highly relevant Indian/Japanese names appear not to have clear US-listed ordinary/ADR access in the gathered evidence, including RHI Magnesita India, Vesuvius India, Grindwell Norton, Shinagawa Refra, TRL Krosaki and IFGL Refractories; later layers should verify OTC availability before excluding them.

The node appears better expressed through foreign OTC industrial-materials issuers than through US primary exchange names; evidence quality should be upgraded with Indian annual reports, plant-level capex links and customer/project wins.
RMGNF/RHI Magnesita N.V. is the best direct U.S.-accessible reference asset for Indian refractory consolidation, but exposure must be traced through RHI Magnesita India and related-party dynamics.
MTX/Minerals Technologies is the most relevant primary U.S.-exchange underfollowed candidate found so far; key gap is proving India-specific refractory systems exposure.

MCRUF/Morgan Advanced Materials is a speculative OTC shadow candidate because its thermal-products portfolio overlaps high-temperature industrial processes, but India steel/cement linkage is unverified.
Tata Steel capacity expansion is useful as a customer-demand anchor for refractory suppliers; use plant-level procurement/tender searches to identify embedded refractory vendors.
The U.S.-listed universe for Indian refractory consolidation is sparse; later layers should include India-listed names and private/unlisted suppliers if mandate permits non-U.S. assets.

RHHMY is the closest US-accessible proxy discovered for Indian refractory consolidation because it is the OTC ADR of RHI Magnesita N.V., parent of RHI Magnesita India, which is described as a leading Indian high-grade refractory supplier.
CKSNY should be tracked as a second organized refractory/flow-control platform with Vesuvius India exposure, especially for steel continuous-casting consumables and advanced refractories.
MTX is a less obvious NYSE-listed mid-cap angle through Minteq and High-Temperature Technologies; India linkage exists in historical source material but needs current-segment verification.

Most direct Indian refractory producers are India-listed rather than US-listed; US mapping requires OTC ADRs or adjacent suppliers. Later layers should not overstate liquidity or index eligibility for OTC names.
GrafTech is not a refractory company and remains only a speculative adjacent steel-consumables shadow candidate unless Indian EAF customer exposure is verified.
